findings.problem: Local packaging accepts an older same-version executable; even a missing ProductVersion passes prepare_portable's conditional. Signature integrity does not bind artifacts to the intended source revision. Fresh CI ordering reduces this risk but the documented standalone local path is unprotected.
findings.observation: Existing target/release/atsumi.exe has ProductVersion2.2.1,76685824bytes and2026-10-13 03:17:33KST modification time, while current Pixiv source changed at18:12:10KST and source version remains2.2.1. No new package was made. Existing default output refusal prevents overwriting the old release but a new output directory can still package that old executable.
findings.smallestPlan: Require a successful-build provenance record binding current version, commit plus source-input/lock/config/resource hashes, target and executable hash. Validate that record immediately before copying/signing installer and portable outputs. Reject absent version, stale source/resource digest or a changed executable. Use a new staging directory, not deletion of existing artifacts. Do not rely only on modification times or commit ID with dirty sources.

findings.severity: P1 release gate; redistribution review incomplete
findings.problem: The pipeline includes license texts but does not stage or publish an exact-version corresponding-source/build-material index or source assets for the redistributed FFmpeg/library and yt-dlp bundled binaries. Existing THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES explicitly leaves this review incomplete. yt-dlp's bundled notice offers upstream-project sources/maintainer contact, which has not been checked as a complete durable delivery route for this distribution. Deno's top-level MIT text is present, but its bundled third-party notice coverage is unverified.
findings.smallestPlan: Before a new release, inventory exact binary components and accepted license route; pin and retain applicable exact corresponding sources, third-party dependency versions, patches and build recipes, with a readable source index next to binary downloads. A separate source asset can avoid bloating the updater ZIP. Keep all required notices and do not claim that distributing only upstream LICENSE or the Atsumi repository supplies every binary's source. This is an engineering release-blocker assessment, not a completed legal opinion.

findings.problem: prepare_media_tools compares only bin EXE/DLL entries, while the packager recursively copies the entire resource directories. A reused package can therefore have missing/changed FFmpeg LICENSE or other non-bin files, or unexpected root files, despite the comment claiming all license files are validated. Platform license files are pinned individually, but extra root/license-directory entries are not rejected. No such tampering was found or performed; this is a code-path gap.
findings.smallestPlan: Create an exact positive manifest for all shipped resource entries including licenses/docs; verify size/hash/type/ancestor boundary before a fresh staging copy and validate the resulting ZIP manifest. Reject unknown/missing files without deleting them. Keep DLL validation and the legacy media-tools root.

findings.problem: The root THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES file is not a configured resource or public frontend asset. public/licenses contains six texts:Apache-2.0,chrono,fs2,hls.js,tauri,tungstenite. No explicit full dependency-notice aggregation is present in the examined build/packaging path; the assertion that normal Cargo/pnpm distribution includes all notices is not backed by that path. Source-package license files existing in node_modules/vendor do not by themselves prove delivery in the app bundle.
findings.smallestPlan: Generate a version-locked runtime dependency notice bundle, including packaged frontend dependencies regardless of devDependency classification (hls.js), Rust/vendor changes and copied icon/decoder notices. Include the reviewed file in public/licenses or a legacy-compatible media-tools/licenses resource and verify it from the final artifact. Inventory first; do not claim every existing dependency is currently missing or infer a license from package name.

findings.problem: Optional WebView2/ is accepted by the portable packager but rejected as an unknown top-level root by existing/current updater extraction. Signing this optional-runtime ZIP and publishing it as the single portable updater artifact would fail. Default CI does not supply the parameter, so its ordinary ZIP is unaffected.
findings.smallestPlan: Explicitly distinguish an initial-install runtime-inclusive package from the legacy-compatible updater ZIP; never feed WebView2/ through the latter. Preserve an already-present runtime during updates and retain browser sandbox requirements. Inspect clean-PC missing-runtime behavior before claiming no external prerequisites.
